questions.question: Q: What are the key stages in planning a citizenship action?

points.text: 1) Identify a citizenship issue, 2) Research the issue thoroughly, 3) Set clear aims and SMART targets, 4) Decide on methods and actions, 5) Plan resources, timescales, and roles, 6) Carry out the action, 7) Evaluate the impact and reflect on learning.

questions.question: Q: Why is it important to identify stakeholders when planning citizenship action?

points.text: Stakeholders are the people or groups affected by or with power over the issue. Identifying them helps you understand who to influence, who to involve, and who might support or oppose your action, making your campaign more strategic and effective.

questions.question: Q: Give an example of a SMART target for a citizenship action.

points.text: To collect 200 signatures on a petition for improved recycling facilities in the school by the end of November, present it to the school council in December, and achieve a commitment from the headteacher by the end of term.

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: To plan a citizenship action on a local issue such as lack of youth facilities, I would first research the issue by surveying young people in my area and gathering data on existing facilities and funding. I would identify which local authority department is responsible and who the relevant decision-makers are. Next, I would set SMART targets: to collect 300 signatures on a petition within three weeks, present findings to the local council within six weeks, and secure a meeting with the cabinet member for communities within two months. I would plan my methods: creating an online petition, running a social media campaign, organising a community meeting, and writing to my local councillor. I would recruit volunteers, assign roles, and set a budget for materials. Finally, I would plan for obstacles — if the council is unresponsive, I would escalate by contacting the local MP or newspaper. Throughout, I would document evidence including petition signatures, meeting notes, and media coverage.
